مَعْقُولٌ [pass. part. n. of عَقَلَ in all its senses as a trans. verb. ―
-b2- Hence it signifies Intellectual, as meaning perceived by the intellect; and excogitated: thus applied as an epithet to any branch of knowledge that is not necessarily مَنْقُولٌ, which means “ desumed, ” such as the science of the fundamentals of religion, and the like. ―
-b3- Hence also, Intelligible. ―
-b4- And Approved by the intellect; or reasonable. ＝
-A2- It is also said to be an inf. n.]: see 1, latter half. ―
-b2- And see عَقْلٌ, latter half, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
